papers.title: Selling China’s story: the multimodal semiotics of positive symbolic communication in national image building through Laowai Wanghong’s vlogs
papers.authors: Luanying Li, Xiaoping Wu, and Richard Fitzgerald
papers.category: 甲亢哥访华 · direct foreign-vlogger China representation
papers.evidence: Publisher or authoritative index record verified
papers.takeaway: A multimodal critical discourse analysis examines how foreign internet celebrities use YouTube videos to represent China through modern factories, cultural richness, and a foreigner-friendly environment. The study finds that these portrayals are curated and filtered and often align implicitly with state-led image-building themes. It is directly relevant to foreign creators visiting and narrating China, but its primary evidence concerns content strategies rather than causal changes in followers’ attitudes.

papers.title: Nation branding via sportswashing: An exploration of pro-China YouTube influencers and commenters around the 2022 Winter Olympic Games
papers.category: 甲亢哥访华 · adjacent China-influencer audience mechanism
papers.evidence: Publisher or authoritative index record verified
papers.takeaway: The study analyzes 27 videos from eight pro-China YouTube channels and 21,958 comments surrounding the 2022 Beijing Winter Olympics. It identifies strategies for building a desirable national brand and countering unfavorable perceptions, then compares engagement and language patterns across likely ordinary users and potentially coordinated accounts. The article offers direct evidence on foreign-facing influencer content, audience engagement, and China’s national image, while the state-linked sports campaign differs from an independent creator visit such as IShowSpeed’s.

papers.title: Generative AI, Job Satisfaction and Type of Work
papers.category: Workplace AI and well-being · direct job-satisfaction evidence
papers.evidence: Publisher or authoritative index record verified
papers.takeaway: A survey of 433 white-collar employees in Poland’s financial-services sector uses ordered logit models to relate generative-AI conditions to job satisfaction. Organizational support and leadership effectiveness are positively associated with satisfaction, whereas individual enthusiasm toward GenAI is not. AI-related technostress is more strongly associated with lower satisfaction in roles highly exposed to AI-driven task transformation, indicating that workplace context and job design shape whether GenAI becomes a resource or a demand.

papers.title: The impact of generative AI use on employees’ psychological distress: a moderated mediation model
papers.authors: M. Liu, Y. Li, and J. Li
papers.category: Workplace AI and well-being · direct psychological-distress evidence
papers.evidence: Publisher or authoritative index record verified
papers.takeaway: Using survey data from 424 Chinese employees, this study tests a moderated mediation model linking workplace GenAI use to psychological distress. Job insecurity and workplace loneliness carry the positive association between use and distress, while information literacy and perceived AI ethical risk operate as boundary conditions. The results provide direct evidence of strain pathways, although the cross-sectional self-report design does not establish that GenAI use itself causes distress.

papers.title: A Game Sense Theory Approach to Translating Culturally Specific Chinese Video Games
papers.category: Preprint · dissertation translation and reception · not peer reviewed
papers.evidence: Publisher or authoritative index record verified
papers.takeaway: This working paper uses translator interviews and player-reception data to examine how culturally specific Chinese video games are localized. It argues that foreignizing strategies predominate for cultural content, while more domesticating strategies are used for interactive terms such as items and skills. Excessive transliteration is associated with less favorable player reception. The paper directly links translation choices to reception of Chinese mythological and cultural material but has not completed journal peer review.

papers.title: Investigating the relationship between generative AI usage and wellbeing: a multi-dimensional analysis of work and private life
papers.authors: Shinichi Yamaguchi, Hidetaka Oshima, Yukiko Osaka, and Tomoaki Watanabe
papers.category: Preprint · workplace GenAI and multidimensional well-being · not peer reviewed
papers.evidence: Publisher or authoritative index record verified
papers.takeaway: Using a large-scale Japanese survey, this working paper examines how GenAI use and use frequency relate to multiple dimensions of well-being and distinguishes work from private use. Work-related use is more strongly associated with life satisfaction, self-realization, and growth, whereas private use is more strongly associated with positive affect, social connection, and gratitude. The observational associations are context-dependent and the paper has not completed journal peer review.

toc.title: The sequential replicant effect in interpersonal sincerity: evidence from AI-mediated apology and gratitude
toc.abstractEn: Across two preregistered, two-wave experiments, cues that artificial intelligence had assisted with apologies or expressions of gratitude consistently reduced perceived sincerity. Making AI mediation salient in an earlier message also increased suspicion of AI use and shaped evaluations of a later message that contained no AI cue, producing a sequential replicant effect.

toc.title: The link between three smartphone school policies and students’ mental health: a growth trajectory approach
toc.abstractEn: Students in three Belgian schools were followed for as many as seven survey waves after the schools adopted different smartphone policies. At baseline, depression and anxiety were highest in the school with a full ban, but trajectories of mental health did not differ significantly across schools. Depressive symptoms increased within both the full-ban school and the school allowing lunchtime use.

papers.title: How does the Chinese animation Ne Zha 2 journey to the world?—From the perspective of Intercultural New Media Studies
papers.category: Dissertation · direct overseas reception of Chinese mythology
papers.evidence: Publisher or authoritative index record verified
papers.takeaway: This mixed-methods case study develops an Intercultural Communication Diamond Model and examines news reports, X posts, YouTube comments, and Reddit discussions about Ne Zha 2. It finds platform-specific reception: X decentralizes conventional gatekeeping, YouTube content fits audience preferences but language barriers limit emotional resonance, and Reddit supports participatory meaning-making. The evidence directly concerns overseas reception of a Chinese mythological character, although it does not isolate understanding, liking, identification, and sharing intention as separate causal outcomes.

papers.title: Recognizing beauty, engaging with goodness, and approaching truth: foreign players’ cross-cultural identification with Chinese culture through Black Myth: Wukong
papers.evidence: Publisher or authoritative index record verified
papers.takeaway: Using foreign-player and critic reviews, this study combines Scene Theory with the Cultural Iceberg Model to describe a three-level path of cross-cultural identification. Players first recognize aesthetic beauty, then engage with moral context and identity formation, and finally approach deeper cultural meanings, although deep identification remains partial. Narrative complexity and cross-cultural misunderstanding constrain reception, making this article directly relevant to distinguishing surface appreciation from deeper character and cultural identification.
